calculation_handling.description: Maximum FSI in the R zone is the value following "d" in the zone label.
Where the zone label has no "d" value, maximum FSI is 0.6.

evidence.semi_detached_houseplex: semi-detached houseplex or a residential building

calculation_handling.description: The FSI limits in (1)(A) and (1)(B) do not apply to a detached houseplex, a semi-detached houseplex or a residential building with a secondary suite.
calculation_handling.gaps: Displaces 10.10.40.40(1)(A) and (1)(B). The secondary-suite arm is an alternative (or) to the houseplex types, so has_secondary_suite is recorded in application only, not as a (conjunctive) condition.

calculation_handling.description: The FSI limits do not apply to a townhouse, or an apartment building with 60 or fewer dwelling units, on a lot abutting a major street.
calculation_handling.gaps: Read conservatively as the 60-unit cap applying to both listed types (the text can also be read as limiting only the apartment building). Requires major street status of the lot.

calculation_handling.description: A pre-October 15, 1953 detached or semi-detached house on a lot with permitted FSI 0.6 may get a rear addition if overall FSI including the addition does not exceed 0.69.
calculation_handling.gaps: Applies only to a detached or semi-detached house erected before October 15, 1953 on a lot whose permitted FSI is 0.6; the 0.6 is the permitted FSI used to decide whether the rear-addition allowance applies, not a limit. Depends on the existing building's construction date and prior additions, which we do not hold. The 0.69 is a ceiling on the permission, not a general FSI limit, so it is not keyed as an fsi LIMIT.

units.disclosure: Older houses (built before October 15, 1953) on 0.6 FSI lots may add a rear addition up to an overall FSI of 0.69; we do not evaluate this because it depends on the age of the existing house.

calculation_handling.description: The rear addition may be no closer to a side lot line than the existing side main wall.
calculation_handling.gaps: Applies only to a detached or semi-detached house erected before October 15, 1953 on a lot whose permitted FSI is 0.6; the 0.6 is the permitted FSI used to decide whether the rear-addition allowance applies, not a limit. Depends on the existing building's construction date and prior additions, which we do not hold.

units.disclosure: The rear-addition allowance for older houses requires the addition to stay within the existing side wall lines; we do not evaluate it.

calculation_handling.description: The rear-addition allowance requires any prior addition to be at least 5 years old.
calculation_handling.gaps: Applies only to a detached or semi-detached house erected before October 15, 1953 on a lot whose permitted FSI is 0.6; the 0.6 is the permitted FSI used to decide whether the rear-addition allowance applies, not a limit. Depends on the existing building's construction date and prior additions, which we do not hold. The 5 years is an age test on prior additions; no DSL variable.

units.disclosure: The rear-addition allowance for older houses requires any earlier addition to be at least 5 years old; we do not evaluate it.

10.10.40.40(1).explanation: In the R zone the maximum floor space index is the "d" number in the zone label, or 0.6 if there is none. This limit does not apply to houseplexes or houses with a secondary suite, nor to townhouses and apartment buildings of up to 60 units on a major street.

10.10.40.40(2).explanation: On a lot with a 0.6 FSI limit, a detached or semi-detached house built before October 15, 1953 may add a rear addition up to an overall FSI of 0.69, if it stays within the existing side walls and any earlier addition is at least 5 years old.
